mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous two-week increases in TRANSIT, WORKPLACES and PARKS mark a self-reinforcing out-of-home recovery that lifts aggregate footfall, carrying RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -39.3 to -33.9 over t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not above the last-28-day mean of -37.2 while TRANSIT, WORKPLACES and PARKS all keep rising week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL falls below 17.0 households have shifted a decisive share of waking hours out of the home, so discretionary retail-and-recreation footfall rises within the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 19.4 at t-2w to 16.9 at t-0w, crossing 17.0
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL prints below 17.0, RETAIL_REC shows no rise within the following two weeks relative to its level at the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT recovery only converts into retail footfall when WORKPLACES return in the same week; the joint rise since t-2w generates commuter-linked retail demand that lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rose in each of the last two weeks
failure_condition: In weeks when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve, the follow-on 28-day RETAIL_REC mean fails to exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under phased reopening with standing capacity caps, TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are the binding policy signal: a weekly TRANSIT gain of two points or more shows restrictions loosening, and RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean improves by 2.0 points or more versus the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 2.7 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of a TRANSIT improvement of 2.0 points or more while capacity caps remain in force.

mechanism_narrative: Late-August seasonal rotation: outdoor recreation demand peaks and then plateaus as the summer ends, shifting discretionary spending indoors, so RETAIL_REC holds above its last-28-day mean over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -38.4 at t-2w to -31.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC falls below -37.2 while PARKS levels off or declines from its t-0w reading.

mechanism_narrative: Standing capacity caps pin RETAIL_REC near its -34 ceiling; the t-2w trough to t-0w rebound is noise reversion around that ceiling, so the next 28-day mean does not exceed the last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly change falls below +1.0 point
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly gains shrank to 2.9 points at t-0w while TRANSIT gained 2.7
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds -37.2, showing recovery continued past the presumed capacity ceiling.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS rising above -32 signals that outdoor mobility has normalized enough for consumers to resume discretionary trips; retail footfall follows within one week with a higher RETAIL_REC print.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS crossed -32.0 at t-0w with a reading of -31.3
failure_condition: In the week after PARKS prints above -32.0, RETAIL_REC does not register a higher weekly mean than in the crossing week.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GROCERY_PHARM trips combined with RESIDENTIAL at or below 17.0 show households widening their errand scope; this interaction converts essential-trip habit into broader retail footfall over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM at or above +6.0 and RESIDENTIAL at or below 17.0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached +8.7 in the same week RESIDENTIAL fell to 16.9
failure_condition: In weeks where GROCERY_PHARM is at or above +6.0 and RESIDENTIAL is at or below 17.0, the following 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not above the prior 28-day mean.
